Kimberly — thanks for the call this morning. As promised, I wanted to give a concise view of where we landed on forecasted load and a few operational constraints so you can propose options we can present to our procurement team next week:

- Expected steady-state: 18 concurrent realtime inference lanes (p50 latency target 150ms), burst to ~36 for 30–45 minutes during nightly processing windows.
- Model mix: 60% 7B decoder-only for chat, 40% 13B encoder-decoder for batch rerank. KV cache reuse is high for chat sessions (~65%).

- Timing: procurement wants a 2-week window to review options; target contract effective 2027-01-01 if we proceed.

Can you send 2–3 reservation structures (minimum GPUs, ramp schedule, activation milestones) so we can decide which to take to procurement?

Thanks — Aisha

Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity needs for inference pipelines — draft options

Team — forwarding Celestia's ask. Drafting three distinct reservation structures that balance cost and SLOs. Key constraints: p50 150ms, burst to 36 lanes, high KV reuse.

Initial thoughts (high level):
- Option A (Conservative baseline): 8 x A100-80GB equivalent GPUs, pinned, with autoscale burst pool to 16 GPUs for scheduled windows. Min GPU floor: 8. Ramp: 0% → 100% over 4 weeks after contract start.
- Option B (Balanced ramp): 12 x A100-80GB equivalent GPUs reserved, with policy to allow on-demand 8 additional GPUs during tight windows (soft burst). Min GPU floor: 12. Ramp: 50% active at day 1, 100% by week 6 (stitch with customer activation milestones).
- Option C (Throughput-first): 20 x A100-80GB equivalent GPUs reserved (higher commit), enables sustained 36 concurrent lanes and reduces per-token cost. Min GPU floor: 20. Ramp: phase in 30%/30%/40% over 90 days.

I want to validate assumptions on concurrency→GPU mapping and whether we should model a quantized variant for batch reranks (saves ~30% GPU memory / 22% token-cost). Ben — can you run a quick capacity model with Celestia mix and KV reuse before EOD? Priyom — I'll need recommended ramp milestones we can include in the SLAs (activation checklist + rollback triggers).

-Kim

Kim, Grace — ran an initial sim with Celestia's mix (60% 7B chat, 40% 13B rerank), KV hit 65% for chat. Summary below (assumptions: A100-80GB perf = baseline unit):

- Mapping: ~2.2 chat lanes / GPU sustained at p50=150ms with 65% KV reuse; rerank jobs are batch-oriented and can be multiplexed — ~3.5 rerank jobs / GPU when quantized variant used.
- Option A (8 GPUs): max sustained concurrent lanes ~17 (close to 18) but relies on scheduled burst pool to hit 36; risk: higher latency during unplanned spikes. Estimated per-token cost: $0.65 (hosted-dedicated adjusted).
- Option B (12 GPUs): comfortable steady-state headroom (24 lanes sustained), bursts to 36 via on-demand gives balanced economics. Per-token cost: $0.52.
- Option C (20 GPUs): supports 36 lanes with margin and reduces per-token cost to $0.41 but increases committed monthly spend by ~60% vs B.

Recommendation: present all three but flag Option B as the pragmatic winner for Celestia given procurement timeline. Also include a quantization recommendation for the rerank model — enables them to choose Option A with lower risk if they adopt quantization early.

-Ben

Adding ramp-playbook language and activation milestones below for inclusion in the proposal (short bullets suitable for an SOW):

- Activation sprint (Day 0–14): provisioning, network peering validation, model staging, and smoke tests. Target: 50% of reserved capacity warmed (for Option B this is 6 GPUs active).
- Secondary ramp (Day 15–45): performance tuning, KV cache warm-up, and load-testing to reach 80% of capacity. Customer acceptance test (CAT) completed at Day 30 to trigger billing of next tranche.
- Full activation (Day 46–90): 100% of reserved capacity in-production. Automatic rollback rules if p50 latency exceeds 200ms for >15 minutes during stress tests.
- Cutover checklist: infra runbook, escalation contacts, fallback to smaller-model (quantized) variants if memory pressure observed.

I'll add specific SLAs for activation acceptance and suggested credits for delayed activation (e.g., 1 week credit per missed milestone). Priyom
